docs.title: Cobblemon HMs
docs.text:
Your Pokémon lend you their moves. Send one out and it cuts trees, smashes rocks and lights caves with your bare fist, gives you auras like Flash, Dive and Rock Climb while it stays near you, or brings its own weather.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started Every HM

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Send out a Pokémon and open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it.
  2. Pick Field moves: it lists every HM whose move that Pokémon has learned.
  3. Partner HMs go to your empty fist: one at a time, fired with a click.
  4. Auras and weather run on you while the Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks.
  5. Mount toggles help the Pokémon itself while you ride it.
  6. Nothing to learn and nothing to carry. Working makes the Pokémon hungry, so keep a few berries on you.

4.0: the companion model

Ditto HMs is now Cobblemon HMs. You no longer learn HMs: every HM comes from a Pokémon of yours that knows the move, working costs it fullness, the Trainer Ditto sells TMs, and the HM Case is a TM bag. What changed.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Download Modrinth · CurseForge · What changed Version 4.0.0 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ — on 1.7.x it refuses to load with a dependency error, not a crash mid-session Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin, Cloth Config NeoForge Kotlin for Forge Optional Mod Menu: the settings screen, on Fabric · Cloth Config: the settings screen, on NeoForge

One jar per loader. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
The command root is /hms.

Who Commands 🙂 Every player list · mount 🛡️ Operators (level 2) list <player> · config … · trader …

There are no commands to learn, select or use an HM any more: your Pokémon lend them, from Cobblemon's interaction wheel (see Your Pokémon).

docs.title: Player commands
docs.text:
/hms list
Shows what your Pokémon are lending you right now: the HM on your fist and the auras in effect.

/hms mount
Reports what the mount boosts can see on the Pokémon you are riding. Useful for telling a broken boost apart from riding something you did not expect.

docs.title: Operator commands
docs.text:
Require permission level 2.

/hms list <player>
The same report, for another player.

/hms trader spawn [player]
/hms trader spawn shiny [player]
/hms trader forget [player]
Summons a Trainer Ditto on demand, or undoes a catch so it will visit that player again.

/hms config                                  every HM and the move behind it
/hms config show                             every world-wide setting at once
/hms config <ability>                        that HM's values, next to the defaults
/hms config <ability> cooldown <ticks>       partner HMs (0–72000) and Sweet Scent (100–72000)
/hms config <ability> power <value>          only HMs that read it, in that HM's range
/hms config <ability> minlevel <0–100>
/hms config <ability> enabled <true|false>
/hms config <ability> fullness <0–700|default>   that HM's upkeep, in hundredths of fullness
/hms config <ability> friendship <0–255|default> friendship it costs per missing fullness point
/hms config <ability> reset
/hms config reset_all

/hms config activator button <left|right|either>
/hms config requiremove <true|false>
/hms config hud <true|false>

/hms config upkeep                           opens the per-HM upkeep table
/hms config upkeep enabled <true|false>
/hms config upkeep use <0–700>               fullness per use, in hundredths
/hms config upkeep minute <0–700>            fullness per minute kept on, in hundredths
/hms config upkeep friendship <0–255>        friendship lost per missing fullness point
/hms config upkeep minfriendship <0–255>     below this a Pokémon refuses HMs (0 = never)

/hms config trader enabled <true|false>
/hms config trader every <1200–1728000>
/hms config trader stay <200–72000>
/hms config trader ivs <0–6>
/hms config trader levels <min> <max>
/hms config trader coins <min> <max>
/hms config trader reload                    re-read trader_offers.json

Every value and its range is in Configuration. The same settings are in the config screen on Fabric and NeoForge.

After updating to 4.0

There is nothing to reset. Every save is migrated the first time each player joins — see Upgrading to 4.0. Retired HMs no longer answer any command.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Starts as the built-in defaults
  2. Saved in config/cobblemon_hms.json
  3. Changed with the Cloth Config screen or /hms config
  4. Result the per-ability values the game uses

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
A partner HM fires from your empty hand: there is nothing to hold and nothing to select. The one choice left is the button:

Setting Options Notes Activator button Left-click · Right-click · either (default) Left never opens chests or doors; right is answered by interactable blocks first 
/hms config activator button left|right|either

Two more switches sit next to it:

Setting Default What it does Pokémon must have learned the move on A Pokémon offers an HM only if it has learned the move, equipped or not. Off: the move in its learnset, or its species, is enough Show active HMs on the HUD on The list of HMs in effect in the top-left corner. A client setting: each player's own file decides 
/hms config requiremove <true|false>
/hms config hud <true|false>

docs.title: Pokémon upkeep
docs.text:
Working costs the Pokémon doing it. Each use of an HM it lends, and every minute an aura, a weather or a ridden mount toggle of its stays on, takes some of its fullness. At 0 fullness it keeps working, but what it cannot pay comes out of its friendship, and below a threshold it refuses to do HMs until that goes back up. Feed it a berry to top it up.

Setting Default What it does HMs cost the Pokémon fullness on Off: HMs cost the Pokémon nothing Fullness per use 25 hundredths Four uses to a berry. A Pokémon holds 2 to 7 points, by weight Fullness per minute kept on 20 hundredths A berry every five minutes, for each HM kept on Friendship lost per missing fullness 5 0 = working hungry costs nothing. Friendship goes up to 255 Friendship needed to do HMs 1 Refuses at 0 friendship · 0 = never refuses 
/hms config upkeep enabled <true|false>
/hms config upkeep use <0-700>
/hms config upkeep minute <0-700>
/hms config upkeep friendship <0-255>
/hms config upkeep minfriendship <0-255>

docs.title: Upkeep for each HM
docs.text:
Every HM can have its own fullness cost and friendship loss. /hms config upkeep on its own opens a table of every HM with its two numbers, on Fabric and NeoForge alike; change what you like and save it in one go. An HM nobody tuned follows the world-wide numbers above.

From the command line, one HM at a time:

/hms config <ability> fullness <0-700|default>     hundredths, per use or per minute kept on
/hms config <ability> friendship <0-255|default>   lost per missing fullness point

Partner HMs pay per use; auras, weather and mount toggles pay per minute they stay on. The table is the server's config: only an operator can open it, and on a dedicated server it edits the server's file, not yours.

docs.title: Trainer Ditto
What it sells
docs.text:
It lays out six random Cobblemon TMs, rolled once and kept for as long as that trader is standing there, one of each. Every price and how often each TM turns up are in config/cobblemon_hms/trader_offers.json. Edit it and run /hms config trader reload to apply it without a restart.

The file is written the first time anyone trades, once Cobblemon has loaded its TMs. The shipped prices follow the level Pokémon learn the move at (the median across species), and the later a move comes, the dearer and rarer its TM:

Move learned at Price Weight below level 30 relic coins, from the TM price band (4 to 32) 10 30 to 39 1 relic coin pouch 6 40 to 49 2 relic coin pouches 4 50 to 59 1 relic coin sack 2 60 and up, or never by level-up (TM-only moves) 1 sack + 2 pouches 1

A weight is relative, not a percentage: a coin TM is ten times as likely to be drawn as a TM-only one. Each entry takes one or two {item, count} costs (the two slots of a trade screen) by item id, so a pack can price in any item it likes. A TM missing from the file is never offered.

It stops visiting a player for good once they catch it, and it keeps its distance from anyone who has caught one or beaten one in battle, so bring a friend who has done neither.

docs.title: Per-ability values
docs.text:
Each HM has only the values it actually reads:

Parameter Which HMs Description Enabled all Off: no Pokémon offers it on its wheel Required level all Experience level needed before the HM works for you (every HM ships at 0) Cooldown partner HMs, and Sweet Scent Ticks between uses (20 ticks = 1 second; 0 = no cooldown), counted per Pokémon. For Sweet Scent it is the time between arrivals, at least 100 Power the HMs in the tables below that list a range What it means depends on the HM: a radius, a duration, a speed in tenths. The menu's tooltip and the command say which Fullness / Friendship all That HM's own upkeep; see Upkeep for each HM

Auras and mount toggles have no cooldown: they are simply on. Nothing costs the player hunger: the Pokémon pays in fullness. The cooldown belongs to the Pokémon that lent the move, so a second Pokémon with the same move is ready straight away.

docs.title: Required level
docs.text: A requirement, not a price: nothing is deducted when the HM fires, you simply cannot reach for it until you have got there. Every HM ships at 0, so nothing is gated unless a pack says so. Switching an aura off is never gated, so raising a requirement can never strand someone inside an effect they cannot end.

docs.title: Config screen
docs.text:
The same Cloth Config screen on both loaders (it needs Cloth Config):

  • Fabric: Mod Menu → Cobblemon HMs → ⚙
  • NeoForge: Mods → Cobblemon HMs → Config

Categories: Activation, Pokémon upkeep, Trainer Ditto, then one per HM. On NeoForge it needs Cloth Config, which is optional there: without it there is no Config button, and /hms config does everything. Short ranges are sliders. Cooldowns, long durations and the Trainer Ditto's timers are typed in, with the same ranges as the command. Each reset arrow goes back to the shipped value. In singleplayer, saving applies at once.

On a dedicated server the screen edits your own game's file, not the server's. Use /hms config there.

docs.title: In-game commands
docs.text:
Operator-only (permission level 2):

/hms config                      lists every HM with the move behind it
/hms config show                 every world-wide setting at once
/hms config <ability>            that HM's values, next to the defaults
/hms config <ability> cooldown <ticks>
/hms config <ability> power <value>
/hms config <ability> minlevel <0–100>
/hms config <ability> enabled <true|false>
/hms config <ability> reset
/hms config reset_all

cooldown and power only exist for an HM that reads them, and each takes the range in the tables below. The full list is in Commands.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
The file is saved at config/cobblemon_hms.json on both loaders.

You can edit it directly. Changes take effect on next server start. It holds only the settings the mod reads. The ones from before 4.0 (hunger costs, blocked hunger, trader weights, cost order, experience per hunger point, activator item, same-move teachers, wheel icon scale) are dropped the next time it is saved. The Trainer Ditto's prices live in their own file, config/cobblemon_hms/trader_offers.json.

docs.title: Default values — Partner HMs
docs.text:
Durations are in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second), because that is what the config takes.

Ability Cooldown Power Power range Leafage 40 (2s) burst radius — 3 (a 7×7 patch) 1–16 Cut none most blocks felled — 128 1–256 Rock Smash none most ore from one vein — 32 1–128 Camouflage 18000 (15 min) ticks in disguise — 18000 20–24000 Strength none — Dig none — Teleport 600 (30s) blocks of reach — 30 5–64 Stockpile 20 (1s) lava self-damage, half hearts — 7 0–40 Charge 60 (3s) ticks between sparks — 10 1–200 Tail Whip none — Growth 1200 (1 min) ticks you stay big — 6000 20–24000 Minimize 1200 (1 min) ticks you stay small — 6000 20–24000 Outrage 6000 (5 min) — Calm Mind 2400 (2 min) — Celebrate none rockets — 8 1–32 Decorate 72000 (1 h) —

Every cooldown takes 0–72000.

docs.text: Ability Power Power range Magnet Rise flight speed, % of walking — 25 10–100 Jump Jump Boost level — 4 1–10 Dive — Flash — Rock Climb — Lava Plume lava-stride multiplier in tenths — 17 10–40 Snowscape trail radius — 3 1–8 Absorb magnet radius — 6 1–24 Lucky Chant Luck level — 1 1–5 Shadow Sneak percent of your speed you keep — 55 10–100 Sweet Scent — · cooldown 1200 (60s) between arrivals, 100–72000 Sandstorm how many times faster loose ground breaks — 4 1–32 Mist blocks away a hunter loses you — 8 2–32 Rain Dance — Thunder — Sunny Day — Blizzard radius of the snowfall around you — 24 2–256

docs.title: Default values — Your Pokémon
docs.text:
Mount toggles belong to the Pokémon you ride.

Ability Power Power range Surf tenths of the mount's swim-speed multiplier — 15 10–50 Agility tenths of the mount's land-speed multiplier — 15 10–50 U-turn tenths of the mount's turn (handling) multiplier, never past the stat's maximum of 100 — 18 10–50 Endure tenths of the mount's Stamina stat, never past 100 — 20 10–50 Tailwind tenths of the mount's flight-speed multiplier — 15 10–50 Swift tenths of the mount's acceleration multiplier — 20 10–50

Old config files

A config written before 4.0 is brought up to date on load, and only where the meaning of a value changed: Teleport's longer cooldown, Tail Whip and Celebrate without one, Decorate's hour, Leafage's 7×7 burst, and Helping Hand's power, which reads backwards as Endure and goes to the new default. A number you set on purpose stays. fog is read as Mist and helping_hand as Endure. Retired HMs (Fly, Glide, Headbutt, Thief and the combat HMs) drop out of the file.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Cobblemon HMs has nothing to learn, craft or carry. Your Pokémon do the work. If a Pokémon of yours has learned a move, it can share it with you while it is out.

docs.title: Your Pokémon's wheel
docs.text:
Send out a Pokémon, open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it and pick Field moves. The wheel that opens lists everything that Pokémon can do for you, and nothing it cannot. Hover a slice and its tooltip says what the HM does.

The slices are grouped by kind, clockwise from the top:

Kind What a pick does Page Partner HM That Pokémon lends the move to your empty fist Partner HMs Aura Switches a passive effect on you, on or off Auras Weather aura Takes over the sky around you; one at a time Auras Mount toggle Helps that Pokémon when you ride it Your Pokémon

A Pokémon can share an HM when it has learned the move: one of its four, or one it learned and later swapped out. It has to be yours, sent out, and within 24 blocks. A server can loosen the rule so that the move in its learnset, or its species, is enough; see Configuration.

Riding your own Pokémon, sneak + right-click opens its Field moves without getting off, so you can switch Surf, Agility and the rest mid-ride.

docs.title: Using a partner HM
docs.text:
Once a Pokémon is lending you an HM, click with an empty hand to fire it. Anything else in your hand keeps its normal click, so tools, weapons and blocks behave exactly as they always did.

One Pokémon lends one HM at a time. Walk away from it and the HM pauses until you are back. Put it back in its ball and it stops lending, and its auras switch off too, weather included: send it out and switch them on again. Mount toggles stay on.

Getting your fist back

While an HM is lent, a bare-handed click fires it instead of punching. Open the Pokémon's wheel and pick the lent move again to hand it back, or simply recall the Pokémon.

The top-left corner of your HUD lists every HM in effect, grouped by kind, with the Pokémon doing each one.

docs.title: What it costs
docs.text:
Nothing costs you anything. The Pokémon pays:

  • Fullness, Cobblemon's berry bar: a quarter of a point each time you fire an HM it lends, and a fifth of a point a minute for each aura, weather or ridden mount toggle it keeps on.
  • A cooldown on some partner HMs, kept per Pokémon, so a second Pokémon with the same move is ready straight away.

Right-click your own Pokémon with any berry to feed it: one berry, one point of fullness. A Pokémon that works on an empty stomach keeps working, but it loses friendship for it, and at 0 friendship it refuses to do HMs. See Your Pokémon.

docs.title: The Trainer Ditto
docs.text:
A rare wandering Trainer Ditto turns up now and then. You hear Ditto's cry when it arrives near you; there is no chat message. Right-click it to open its stall.

  • The first time you meet one, it gives you an HM Case, the bag for your TMs. The Case has no recipe: this is where it comes from.
  • It sells six random Cobblemon TMs a visit, one of each, for relic coins, relic coin pouches and relic coin sacks. The later Pokémon learn a move, the dearer its TM and the rarer it turns up; TMs for moves no Pokémon learns by levelling up are the dearest of all.
  • It turns up at random, about every 30 minutes on average for the whole server, and stays about 5 minutes before it wanders off.

Every price is in a file the server owner can edit; see Configuration.

It is a Ditto in a coat. Throw a Poké Ball and you catch it like any other, but every trader after that keeps its distance and will not open its stall for you again, and beating one in battle does the same, so weigh the shop against the Ditto. How good that Ditto is is the server's call, and out of the box it rolls its IVs like any other: guaranteed perfect stats are an option an operator turns on, not something the trader comes with.

It is shiny at Cobblemon's own odds, and wears a shiny costume. Once caught it is an ordinary, non-shiny Ditto: the shine was the costume, not the prize.

Each trader wears a random player skin, and keeps it for as long as it stands there.

For resource pack makers: adding faces

Every PNG under assets/cobblemon_hms/textures/entity/trainer_ditto/ is in the pool, so a resource pack adds a face by dropping a file in. A file whose name contains shiny is kept for the shiny trader.

docs.title: Your Pokémon
docs.text:
Everything in Cobblemon HMs comes from your Pokémon. Send one out, open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it and pick Field moves. The second wheel lists everything that Pokémon can do for you:

  • Partner HMs it can lend your empty fist: see Partner HMs.
  • Auras and weather it can give you while it is out and near you: see Auras.
  • Mount toggles that help it when you ride it: below.

A Pokémon can do any of these when it has learned the move: one of its four, or one it learned and later swapped out. A server that turns off Pokémon must have learned the move (Configuration) also lets the move in its learnset, or its species (the ones listed on these pages), count.

docs.title: Keeping it fed
docs.text:
Working makes a Pokémon hungry. It pays in fullness, Cobblemon's own berry bar:

What it does What it costs, by default Each time you fire an HM it lends you a quarter of a point of fullness Each minute an aura, a weather or a mount toggle of its stays on (a mount toggle only while you ride it) a fifth of a point, for each one

A Pokémon holds 2 to 7 points of fullness, by its weight, so a berry covers about four uses or five minutes of one aura.

Right-click your own Pokémon with any berry to feed it: one berry, one point of fullness, and you hear it eat. Oran, Sitrus, Lum and the other berries Cobblemon already uses still heal or cure as before when they would, and feed it too. Sneak + right-click still opens the interaction wheel.

At 0 fullness it keeps working, so nothing switches off in the middle of a cave. But each point it cannot pay costs it 5 friendship, and it sulks while that happens. At 0 friendship it refuses to do HMs until its friendship comes back up.

Operators can change every one of these numbers, world-wide or for each HM on its own, or switch the upkeep off: see Configuration.

docs.title: Mount toggles
docs.text:
The toggles that make a ride better belong to the Pokémon you ride. Open the same Field moves wheel on it and switch them on there; a toggle that is on shows green. They stay on for that Pokémon, not for you and not for your other mounts, and help it whenever it is ridden. Putting it back in its ball does not switch them off.

Already riding? Sneak + right-click opens your mount's Field moves without getting off.

Disc Toggle Pokémon (any of) While it is on Surf Lapras, Gyarados, Milotic It cuts through water much faster. Tailwind Pidgeot, Noivern, Staraptor It moves noticeably faster through the air. Swift Ninjask, Accelgor, Electrode It gets up to speed twice as quickly. U-turn Yanma, Ninjask, Venipede It turns far more sharply, on land, in water and in the air, up to the best handling a mount can have. Gliders, helicopters and burst swimmers have no handling stat, so it does nothing for them. Endure Mudbray, Mudsdale, Tauros Its Stamina doubles, up to the best a mount can have (100), so it runs, swims or flies longer before it tires. Agility Arcanine, Zebstrika, Cyclizar It runs faster on land.

The species listed are the ones that can always do it when the server lets species count; any Pokémon that has learned the move can do it.

The Jump and Rock Climb auras also carry over to whatever you are riding.

Endure was Helping Hand

Before 4.0 this toggle was Helping Hand, and it cut how fast the stamina bar drained. It is Endure now and raises the Stamina stat itself. A config file or a save that still says helping_hand is read as Endure.

docs.title: What the Ride tab shows
docs.text: Open the Pokémon's summary while a mount toggle is on and the Ride tab draws what your HMs add as its own layer: the Pokémon's own stats in the usual solid shape, and the boost on top of it in the same colour, lighter, with a dotted outline. The numbers around the chart read the boosted value.

docs.title: HM Case (TM bag)
docs.text:
Since 4.0 the HM Case is a bag for Cobblemon TMs. It holds as many as you like, of as many moves as you like, in one slot.

You get one from the Trainer Ditto the first time you meet one: it is no longer crafted. Right-click with the Case in hand to open it.

Do What happens Put TMs away Every TM in your inventory goes into the bag Click a row Takes one TM of that move out Shift-click a row Takes the whole stack out Type in the search box Filters the list by move name

The Case's tooltip shows how many TMs are inside. A TM taken out that does not fit in your inventory stays in the bag, so nothing is ever dropped.

The contents are stored on the Case itself, so it keeps them when you put it in a chest or hand it to a friend.

Where TMs come from

The Trainer Ditto sells six random TMs for relic coins, pouches and sacks every time it visits.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: The game will not start and names Cobblemon
docs.text: Cobblemon HMs needs Cobblemon 1.8.0 or newer. On 1.7.x it refuses to load with a dependency error rather than crashing mid-session. Update Cobblemon. The rest of what to install is in the table at the bottom of the home page.

docs.title: Two copies of the mod load, or the game crashes on start after updating
docs.text: The 4.0 jar is cobblemon-hms-…; the old one was cobblemon-ditto-hms-…. To the loader they are different mods, so both load. Delete the old jar from mods/. See Upgrading to 4.0.

docs.title: My punches fire an HM
docs.text: While a Pokémon is lending you an HM, a bare-handed click fires it instead of punching. Pick the lent move again in that Pokémon's wheel to hand it back, or recall the Pokémon. See Partner HMs.

docs.title: A Pokémon does not offer an HM
docs.text: By default it has to have learned the move: one of its four, or one it learned and swapped out. A move it could learn but never did does not count, unless the server turned Pokémon must have learned the move off. It also has to be yours, sent out, and within 24 blocks, and the HM has to be enabled on the server.

docs.title: My Pokémon refuses to do HMs
docs.text: Its friendship ran out. HMs cost a Pokémon fullness, and once it is empty each point it cannot pay costs it friendship; at 0 friendship it refuses. Feed it berries (right-click it with any berry) and raise its friendship again. See Keeping it fed.

docs.title: There is no Config button on NeoForge
docs.text: The config screen needs Cloth Config, an optional dependency on NeoForge. Install it, or use /hms config instead, which works without it.

docs.title: An HM I had is gone after updating to 4.0
docs.text: In 4.0 you no longer learn HMs: your Pokémon lend them. Every trigger item you paid is handed back the first time you join, so there is nothing to reset. See Upgrading to 4.0.

docs.title: My old config file changed
docs.text: A config written before 4.0 is brought up to date on load, and only where the meaning of a value changed. Retired HMs drop out of the file. See Configuration.

docs.title: Upgrading to 4.0
docs.text: 4.0 renames the mod to Cobblemon HMs and turns it around: you no longer learn HMs, your Pokémon lend them to you. A Pokémon that has learned the move can share it while it is out and near you, and working costs it fullness. Everything that fights lives in Cobblemon Action Combat.

docs.title: The new name
docs.text:
Up to 3.x the mod was Ditto HMs. 4.0 renames everything, including the mod id (cobblemon_ditto_hms is now cobblemon_hms):

  • The jars are cobblemon-hms-fabric-… and cobblemon-hms-neoforge-…. Delete the old cobblemon-ditto-hms-… jar from mods/ when you update: the loader sees two different mods and would load both.
  • Your world carries over. HM Cases and discs in chests and inventories, everyone's HM save and the config file are read under the old name and saved under the new one.
  • The command is /hms (it was /dittohm).
  • The key binding for the HM wheel goes back to its default once.
  • A new mod icon: the HM Case in the Cobblemon frame, in the mod list of both loaders.

docs.title: Your save
docs.text:
Nothing to do, and nothing you paid for is lost. The first time each player joins after the update:

  • Every HM you had learned is cleared, and its trigger item is handed back, or dropped at your feet if your inventory is full.
  • An old HM disc found in a chest trades for its trigger item when you right-click with it.
  • A chat message explains what happened.

The config file is updated too, and only where a value changed meaning; see Configuration.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
• Nothing to learn. Open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on your Pokémon, pick Field moves, and it lists every HM whose move that Pokémon has learned, sorted by kind. See Getting Started.
  • Partner HMs go to your empty fist, one at a time. See Partner HMs.
  • Auras run while the Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks; weather auras run one at a time. See Auras.
  • Mount toggles belong to the Pokémon you ride. Sneak + right-click while riding opens them. See Your Pokémon.
  • Your Pokémon get hungry, not you. Each use and each minute an aura stays on costs the Pokémon fullness; feed it any berry. Working on an empty stomach costs it friendship, and at 0 friendship it refuses. See Keeping it fed.
  • No HM wheel and no H key. Everything is in the Pokémon's own wheel.
  • A HUD list in the top-left corner shows every HM in effect. Auras are no longer potion effects.
  • The Trainer Ditto sells six TMs a visit for relic coins, pouches and sacks instead of teaching HMs, and gives you an HM Case the first time you meet it.
  • The HM Case is a TM bag with a search box, and is no longer crafted. See HM Case.
  • NeoForge has a config screen, the same one as Fabric's (it needs Cloth Config).

docs.title: What went where
docs.text:
HMs Partner HMs Cut · Rock Smash · Dig · Stockpile · Leafage · Strength · Teleport · Camouflage · Charge · Tail Whip · Growth · Minimize · Outrage · Calm Mind · Celebrate · Decorate Auras Magnet Rise · Rock Climb · Dive · Jump (from Splash) · Flash · Lava Plume · Absorb · Lucky Chant · Shadow Sneak · Snowscape · Sweet Scent Weather auras Rain Dance · Thunder · Sunny Day · Blizzard · new: Sandstorm · Mist Merged X-Scissor → Cut · Rototiller → Leafage (crouch) · Water Gun and Eruption → Stockpile Your mount's toggles Surf · Tailwind · Swift · U-turn · Helping Hand, now Endure · Agility Moved to Cobblemon Action Combat Bullet Seed · Explosion · String Shot · Crabhammer · Mean Look · Harden · Burning Bulwark · Substitute · Destiny Bond · Egg Bomb · Protect · Whirlwind · Barrier · Acid Armor · Rock Throw · Boomerang · Powder Snow · Confusion Retired Fly · Glide · Headbutt · Thief · Present · Miracle Eye · Rest · Defog · Revival Blessing · Charm · Bounce · Obstruct · Ember · Earthquake · Vine Whip · Waterfall

Fly is gone because travelling by air is what your flying Pokémon are for: ride one, with Tailwind on to make it faster. Magnet Rise stays as a slow hover for building.

docs.title: Partner HMs
docs.text:
Partner HMs are the ones your empty fist fires. One of your sent-out Pokémon lends you one: open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on it, pick Field moves, then "Lend me …". While that Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks, a click with an empty hand fires the HM. One Pokémon lends one HM at a time: picking another replaces it.

Each use costs the Pokémon a little fullness (see Keeping it fed). Some HMs also have a cooldown, kept per Pokémon: two Pokémon that both know Teleport each have their own.

  1. Do Click with an empty hand
  2. Check A Pokémon of yours, out and near you, is lending the HM
  3. Check That Pokémon still has friendship (at 0 it refuses)
  4. Check Your experience level is high enough (if the server sets one)
  5. Check That Pokémon's cooldown has run out
  6. Result The HM fires, the Pokémon pays its fullness and its cooldown starts

If any check fails, nothing happens.

docs.title: Who can lend it
docs.text:
A Pokémon can lend an HM when it has learned the move, one of its four or one it swapped out. A move merged into an HM counts for it too, so a Pokémon that knows X-Scissor can lend Cut. On a server that lets species count, these can always lend it:

Disc HM Pokémon (any of) Camouflage Zorua, Kecleon, Ditto Charge Elekid, Electabuzz, Electivire Cut Scyther, Scizor, Kartana, Kleavor, Vikavolt Decorate Sylveon, Milcery, Togekiss Dig Diglett, Dugtrio, Trapinch Leafage Bulbasaur, Chikorita, Treecko, Snivy, Drilbur, Excadrill Rock Smash Hitmonchan, Machop, Geodude Stockpile Gulpin, Swalot, Squirtle, Totodile, Mudkip, Camerupt, Magcargo, Heatran Strength Machoke, Machamp, Conkeldurr Tail Whip Rattata, Sentret, Buneary Teleport Abra, Kadabra, Alakazam, Ralts Growth Sunkern, Sunflora, Petilil Minimize Ditto, Chansey, Barboach Outrage Dragonite, Salamence, Haxorus Calm Mind Alakazam, Espeon, Gardevoir Celebrate Jigglypuff, Ludicolo, Alcremie

docs.title: Camouflage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 15 min · Power: 18000t (15 minutes)

Become the living creature you're looking at. Your model is replaced by theirs — species, form, variant, gear and its nametag — for everyone who can see you. Copy a trainer from Radical Cobblemon Trainers and you wear that trainer's own skin.

  • Aim at a creature in clear view → you look exactly like it for 15 minutes.
  • Fire it again while you are wearing one → the costume comes off and the HM is ready immediately, so changing disguise is two presses.
  • A block, a wall between you and it, or empty air → nothing happens. You can only copy something you can actually see.
  • Other players can't be copied.

The disguise is a costume, not a creature: nothing extra exists in the world, so there is nothing to hit, nothing in your way, and nothing that can be killed off you.

docs.title: Charge
docs.text:
Cooldown: 3s · Power: ticks between sparks (10)

Turns the block you aim at into a redstone power source — enough to throw a door, a piston or a lamp from across a room. The charge is permanent. It is saved with the world, so it stays when you log off and when the server restarts, and charging another block does not take it back: charge as many as you like. Aim Charge at a charged block again to discharge it. Breaking the block ends its charge too.

The block is never replaced — it stays exactly what it is and simply answers as a power source — so you can charge a chest, a furnace, a statue or a wall without losing anything. While it is live it glows with redstone dust on its faces, so a charged block is one you can find again.

docs.title: Cut
docs.text:
Cooldown: none · Power: max 128 blocks

Aim at a log and the tree comes down — its logs, with the leaves and vines tangled in it. Only that one tree: a neighbour whose canopy touches it is left standing, and you hear it fall once, not a hundred break sounds. A log somebody placed, like a cabin wall, comes out on its own. Aim at a leaf or a vine and just that tangle goes.

It also cuts plants: grass, ferns, crops, ground cover. Those come away as if you had used shears, so the drops are the careful ones — the grass itself rather than a couple of seeds — and that holds for plants added by a datapack too, because it is the game's own loot tables answering.

With nothing to cut in front of you, it clears the ground around you (this is what X-Scissor used to do), in two passes of decreasing politeness:

  1. Weeds first — grass, ferns, dead bushes. If there are any, that is all it touches.
  2. Then what somebody planted — flowers and crops, and only once there is not a single weed left in range (radius 5). Casting by accident in your own wheat field costs you the weeds, not the field.

It never strips grass down to dirt: as a fallback, that would go off every time you missed a tree.

docs.title: Leafage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 2s · Power: radius 3 (a 7×7 patch)

Instantly grows every crop around you to full maturity — handy for fast harvests — and does the same for saplings and berry trees.

The bare ground answers too, and it answers in flowers: a burst leaves a meadow rather than a lawn, with the odd blade of grass among it. The blooms are ones that belong to the biome you are standing in, so a burst in a plains looks nothing like one in a flower forest — and a biome with no flowers of its own gets grass rather than a dandelion that does not belong there.

It only ever plants on bare ground. A spot that already has something growing on it is left exactly as it stands, so casting twice in the same meadow thickens it instead of disturbing it, and tall flowers are planted whole rather than as a half that topples.

Only crops, saplings and berry trees are grown. Grass blades, ferns, moss, nylium, glow lichen and seagrass are left alone, so a burst never smothers the meadow it planted or creeps moss over the stone nearby.

Crouch while you use it to till instead (this is what Rototiller used to do): the dirt-type block you aim at, within your normal reach — Dirt, Grass Block, Coarse Dirt, Dirt Path — turns into Farmland. A flower or grass on it drops as an item. Tilling has no cooldown and does not use up the burst's.

It changes the world, so it needs the right to build: it does nothing in adventure or spectator mode, and skips spawn protection and claimed land. The radius (power) is capped at 16.

docs.title: Rock Smash
docs.text:
Cooldown: none · Power: max 32 ores

Instantly breaks the block you aim at. If it's an ore, vein-mines all connected ore of that type; otherwise breaks the single pickaxe-minable block (Netherite Pickaxe drops). Dirt, sand and the rest of what a shovel takes are Dig's.

docs.title: Dig
docs.text:
Cooldown: none

What a shovel takes, dirt, sand, gravel, clay and snow, comes out in one hit, one block per click, with a shovel's drops. Stone and ore stay Rock Smash's.

Dig was folded into Rock Smash early in 4.0 and is its own HM again: one HM that both smashed and dug read as neither.

docs.title: Stockpile
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1s · Power: lava self-damage 7 (3.5 hearts)

Stockpile is a mouthful you keep. It took over Water Gun and Eruption.

  • Aim at water or lava (source or flowing) and you drink it. The pool is drained, and that fluid is now what you carry. Water is free; lava is spicy and burns going down.
  • Aim anywhere else and you spit it back out on the face you are aiming at — the same square a bucket would fill. You can spit as often as you like: what you carry only changes when you drink the other fluid.
  • Spitting water at a sponge soaks it.

It passes the same permission check a bucket does, so claims, spawn protection and the world border all hold. Lava is never placed at your own feet, and water boils away in the Nether, as it would from a bucket.

docs.title: Strength
docs.text:
Cooldown: none

Pushes the aimed block one block in whichever of the six directions you're looking — up and down included. Containers travel with their contents, and a double chest moves as one unit: both halves go together, or the push fails if either has nowhere to go. Won't move fluids.

docs.title: Tail Whip
docs.text:
Cooldown: none

Sweeps a suspicious sand or gravel block clean in a single motion instead of a dozen slow ones, and finds exactly what a brush would have found. Rooted dirt counts too: it is not brushable in vanilla, but it is the same gesture on the same kind of thing, so it gives up its hanging roots. With no cooldown you can sweep a whole row of suspicious sand one click at a time.

docs.title: Teleport
docs.text:
Cooldown: 30s · Power: max 30 blocks

Blinks you to the block you're looking at (≤ 30 blocks), finding the nearest safe landing. Plays the Enderman teleport sound.

It is the strongest way to travel the mod has, so it is priced like it: slow to come back.

docs.title: Growth
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1 min · Power: how long you stay big (5 minutes)

Aim at one of your Pokémon, or a wild one, and it grows one size, for good, and you see it resize on the spot. Aim at anything else, or at nothing, and it is you who grows, to twice your size, for a while.

docs.title: Minimize
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1 min · Power: how long you stay small (5 minutes)

Growth's opposite. Aim at a Pokémon and it shrinks one size, for good. Aim anywhere else and you go half-size for a while.

docs.title: Outrage
docs.text:
Cooldown: 5 min

Aim at an XL Pokémon to turn it into an Alpha. Anything smaller, it refuses.

docs.title: Calm Mind
docs.text:
Cooldown: 2 min

Aim at an Alpha to settle it back into the ordinary Pokémon it was. The way back out of Outrage.

docs.title: Celebrate
docs.text:
Cooldown: none · Power: how many rockets (8)

Punch with an empty hand and a firework show goes up over your head, for no reason at all. The rockets are made for you, not taken from your inventory, and they hurt nobody, even when they burst against a ceiling. There is no cooldown: celebrate as often as you like.

docs.title: Decorate
docs.text:
Cooldown: 1 hour

Aim at one of your Pokémon, or a wild one, for one roll at making it shiny, for good. The odds are Cobblemon's own (1 in 8192 unless the server changed them), so a shiny from Decorate is as rare as one found in the grass. Luck improves them: each level divides the odds, so Lucky Chant at I makes it 1 in 4096.

Another player's Pokémon is refused, and so is the Trainer Ditto.

docs.title: Auras
docs.text:
Auras are passive HMs your Pokémon give you while they are out and near you (24 blocks). Open Cobblemon's interaction wheel on one of your sent-out Pokémon, pick Field moves, and switch an aura on; it shows ✔ while it is on. Walk away from the Pokémon and the aura pauses; it comes back when you do.

You can run as many auras as you like, from one Pokémon or several. Each one costs the Pokémon giving it a little fullness for every minute it stays on (see Keeping it fed).

Put the Pokémon back in its ball and its auras switch off. Sending it out again does not bring them back: switch them on again from its wheel. Walking away from it only pauses them.

The toggles that make a mount better — Surf, Tailwind, Swift, U-turn, Endure and Agility — belong to the Pokémon you ride: see Your Pokémon.

Active HMs on your HUD

The top-left corner of your HUD lists every HM in effect, grouped by kind — Companion (the HM lent to your fist), Aura, Weather and Mount — each with its own icon and the Pokémon doing it in brackets, by its nickname if it has one: for example Sandstorm (Dunes). The interaction wheel shows the same list in its corner. Auras do not show as status effects. Hide the list with Show active HMs on the HUD in the config screen (Mod Menu on Fabric, the mod list's Config button on NeoForge), or /hms config hud false in singleplayer.

docs.title: Weather auras
docs.text:
One weather at a time

Rain Dance, Thunder, Sunny Day, Blizzard, Sandstorm and Mist are weather. Only one runs at a time: switching one on, on any of your Pokémon, switches the others off, so the last one you switched on is the one in effect. Between players close together, too, the weather switched on last wins. Like any aura, a weather only works while its Pokémon is out and near you, and putting the Pokémon back in its ball switches it off.

Every weather takes over Minecraft's own sky while it is on: Rain Dance makes it rain, Thunder brews a thunderstorm, and all the others keep it clear, so no rain falls through your sandstorm, mist or blizzard while their own effects run. Switch it off, or recall the Pokémon, and the game decides the weather again.

Snowscape is not a weather: it is a plain aura (snow underfoot, nothing in the sky), so it runs alongside any of them.

docs.title: Who can give it
docs.text:
A Pokémon can give an aura when it has learned the move, one of its four or one it swapped out. On a server that lets species count, these can always give it:

Disc Aura Pokémon (any of) Absorb Gulpin, Swalot, Victreebel Blizzard (weather) Abomasnow, Glalie, Froslass Dive Vaporeon, Lapras, Wailord Flash Ampharos, Jolteon, Lanturn Jump Magikarp, Buneary, Spoink — or any Pokémon with Splash Lava Plume Magcargo, Slugma, Turtonator Lucky Chant Clefairy, Chimecho, Togetic Magnet Rise Magnemite, Magneton, Magnezone Rain Dance (weather) Politoed, Kyogre, Golduck Rock Climb Rhydon, Rhyperior, Sneasel Shadow Sneak Gengar, Banette, Spiritomb Snowscape Froslass, Mamoswine Sunny Day (weather) Torkoal, Sunkern, Volcarona Sweet Scent Gloom, Bellossom, Vileplume, Aromatisse Thunder (weather) Pikachu, Raichu, Zapdos Sandstorm (weather) Hippopotas, Hippowdon, Tyranitar, Gigalith, Sandaconda Mist (weather) Lapras, Lotad, Lombre, Ludicolo, Suicune — or any Pokémon with Mist

docs.title: Absorb
docs.text:
Power: magnet radius 6

Loose items on the ground drift toward you while it is on, so a scattered drop or a mined vein gathers itself. Items are nudged rather than yanked, so they keep their normal pickup delay.

docs.title: Dive
docs.text:
Lets you live and work underwater. Water stops getting in your way:

  • Breathe underwater — never run out of air.
  • Walk the seabed as if it were dry land — no wading, no drag on every step.
  • Mine at full speed — a block underwater breaks as fast as the same block in open air, and the weight a guardian temple puts on your arms lifts while you're under.

Dive takes penalties away; it never hands out a bonus. Push off the bottom and you swim at exactly the speed you always did — if you want to be fast in the water, ride a Pokémon with Surf switched on.

docs.title: Flash
docs.text: Lets you see clearly in the dark, even in caves and at night. Toggle off to remove instantly. It works with Iris shader packs too: the world itself gets brighter, not just the screen.

docs.title: Jump
docs.text:
Power: Jump Boost level (default IV)

Comes from the move Splash, so any Pokémon that knows it can give it. Applies continuous Jump Boost. The power value equals the buff level, so power = 4 gives Jump Boost IV.

docs.title: Lava Plume
docs.text:
Power: tenths of the movement multiplier (default 17)

Dive's twin for lava. It lets you live and work down there: you do not burn, you move through lava and walk its floor without the fluid dragging on every step, and you breathe while you are under. Swimming out is exactly as it always was — like Dive, it takes a penalty away rather than handing out a bonus.

  • Fire: you are fire immune, like a Strider: no damage, and no flames on your screen or on your body, in lava or out of it.
  • Seeing: with your head under the lava you can see about 24 blocks instead of one, and the floor around you is lit. Wading with your head above the surface leaves the sky as it is.
  • Moving: walking through lava is as quick as walking on land. Sprint and you swim, a little faster, but never faster than you sprint on land.
  • Breathing: your air never runs out while you are under.

Like every aura it only works while its Pokémon is out and within 24 blocks. If it wanders off, goes back in its ball or you switch the aura off, the fire protection lasts 5 more seconds and you get a warning if you are in lava, enough to climb out.

It used to need Burning Bulwark for the fire protection. Burning Bulwark went to Cobblemon Action Combat, so Lava Plume now covers that on its own.

docs.title: Lucky Chant
docs.text: Fortune leans your way while it lasts: what you break and what you fish give up a little more.

docs.title: Magnet Rise
docs.text:
Power: percent of creative flight speed you get (default 25)

Flight. Switch it on and double-tap jump to lift off, as in creative mode. You stay up for as long as you like, drifting at a little over half your walking pace, and sprinting gives no dash. While it is on you take no fall damage.

It is a building tool, not a way to travel: for that, ride one of your flying Pokémon.

  • It ends when the aura does: recall the Pokémon, switch it off, or get more than 24 blocks from it (flying straight up counts). If that happens in the air, you float down on Slow Falling until you land instead of dropping.
  • Logging out while flying is safe: you come back floating down, and switch it on again once your Pokémon is out.
  • It never touches a flight you have from somewhere else (creative mode, another mod, /fly).

docs.title: Rock Climb
docs.text:
Every vertical surface behaves like a ladder, and it is steered by the movement keys: W climbs, S descends, and holding nothing holds your place on the wall.

Your horizontal movement is left alone, so you can travel along a face and step off it whenever you like — a wall is something to climb, not something to be stuck to. On the ground it only takes over when you are actually asking to go up, so walking and jumping near a wall work normally.

It works on your mount too. Riding a Pokémon, run into a wall holding W and your Pokémon climbs it with you.

docs.title: Shadow Sneak
docs.text:
Power: percent of your speed you keep (default 55)

Total stealth on foot. No footstep sounds, no name over your head, and nothing underfoot notices you — not pressure plates, not tripwires, not a sculk sensor.

You move slower than a walk for it, though faster than a crouch, so it is something you can actually travel in rather than a stationary hiding trick. You cannot sprint on land while it runs, and climbing a ladder or vine makes no sound either.

It only works on land: in water or lava you swim at your normal speed, sprint-swimming included.

If you are already on a scoreboard team

The hidden nametag is done with a vanilla team, so a player who already belongs to one keeps their team and simply does not get that part of the effect. Everything else still applies.

docs.title: Snowscape
docs.text:
Power: trail radius 3

Winter follows you on foot: snow settles around you as you walk, and still water freezes over as you cross it, the way Frost Walker does. Flowing water is left alone, so a river keeps running instead of being paved, and the ice melts back once you have passed. Where it is too warm to snow (a desert, a jungle, a plain), the snow melts away again shortly behind you; in a cold biome it stays.

  • It works only on foot: not while you ride, swim or fall, so it never freezes the sea under a Pokémon you are surfing on.
  • Only open water freezes. Kelp, seagrass and waterlogged blocks are left as they are, and no ice forms around a creature standing in the water.
  • It changes only what you could change by hand: nothing in adventure mode, in spectator mode or inside spawn protection, and nothing on land a claim mod protects from you.

It is a plain aura, not a weather, so it runs alongside whichever weather is on.

docs.title: Sweet Scent
docs.text:
Cooldown: 60s between arrivals

Works like a Poké Snack you carry around. While it is on, the Pokémon giving off the scent gives off pink dust, and a wild Pokémon from the area turns up near it about once a minute. It uses Cobblemon's own spawner with the Poké Snack's rules, so what arrives is what lives there, and it never brings a herd.

The held item is the seasoning. Whatever the Pokémon giving off the scent is holding works the way that item would as a Poké Snack seasoning: a berry that leans a snack toward a type, a nature or a shiny leans the scent the same way. Several Pokémon with Sweet Scent on add their items together, like several seasonings in one snack. The item is not used up. A seasoning that makes a snack bite sooner (a bite-time effect) makes the next arrival come sooner too, with the same chance it has in a snack.

Arrivals follow the snack's limits: no more than Cobblemon's Poké Snack cap of wild Pokémon per chunk around you, nothing arrives while you are dead or spectating, and the interval never drops below 5 seconds whatever the config says.

docs.title: Sandstorm
docs.text:
Power: how many times faster loose ground breaks (4)

Weather aura. A sandstorm you can see blows around you, in any biome and any dimension, and every player nearby sees it too. The vanilla sky stays clear. Sand is your ground while it blows:

  • Soul sand and honey never slow you down: you walk on them as fast as on stone. It works in the Nether too, so a soul sand valley is open ground.
  • Sand, gravel, soul sand, soul soil, clay and concrete powder break 4× as fast, whatever you dig them with. Everything else breaks at its normal speed, so it never makes your pickaxe faster.
  • Another player's weather switched on later, close to you, replaces your sandstorm until you move apart or theirs ends.

docs.title: Mist
docs.text:
Power: blocks away a hunter loses you (8)

Weather aura, with a clear sky. A grey mist rolls in around you, the same everywhere, sky included, and you can only see about 20 blocks. Anything hunting you loses track of you once you are more than 8 blocks away, and goes back to wandering. Up close it still sees you, so Mist is for slipping away, not for standing in the open.

Early in 4.0 this aura was called Fog and also came from Haze and Smokescreen; now it comes from the move Mist. A config file that still says fog is read as Mist.

docs.title: Rain Dance
docs.text:
Weather aura. It rains, the game's own rain, for as long as Rain Dance is on and its Pokémon is out. Switch it off or recall the Pokémon and Minecraft takes the weather back.

It rains wherever you are: deserts, snowy biomes, the Nether and the End included. Within 16 blocks of you it is real rain for everything that asks: it puts out fires and burning mobs, lets Riptide work, fills cauldrons, and counts for Cobblemon's rain spawns and rain evolutions.

docs.title: Thunder
docs.text:
Weather aura. It brews a thunderstorm, for as long as Thunder is on and its Pokémon is out. It rains wherever you are, exactly like Rain Dance, with thunder on top.

The moment you switch it on, a bolt comes down 6 to 12 blocks away. That opening bolt is only for show: it flashes and booms but sets nothing alight and hurts nobody, so switching it on next to your own base is safe. The storm's own lightning after that is the game's, and does what vanilla lightning does.

docs.title: Sunny Day
docs.text: Weather aura. The sky stays clear, with no rain and no storms, for as long as Sunny Day is on and its Pokémon is out. Switch it off or recall the Pokémon and Minecraft takes the weather back.

docs.title: Blizzard
docs.text:
Power: radius of the snowfall around you (24)

Weather aura. Snow falls and settles all around you, whatever the biome, for as long as Blizzard is on and its Pokémon is out. The sky stays clear of vanilla rain meanwhile. The snow is real snow: it piles up to three layers and settles where a real snowfall would, on open ground, never on top of flowers or grass and not right next to a torch.

Where it is too warm to snow, the snow melts on its own a few minutes after the storm has moved on or been switched off, even across a server restart. Where the biome is cold enough to snow, it is ordinary snow and stays.

It does not snow in the Nether (there is no sky there, only a roof), and it stops while you are in spectator mode.
